walkthrough: Goal: tune a brush to my hand and keep it: make the Inker's points longer, try a chalky copy of it, and see every change on a sample stroke before I draw on the canvas.

Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library. Tap the Brush button: the Brushes panel lists the brushes; tap Inker to draw with it, then tap Inker again: the panel turns into the Inker's editor in place, as Actions turns into its Pen buttons page. At the top 'Inker' as the heading and Back; under it a paper-white strip with an S-shaped Inker stroke drawn at my size and colour, its pressure rising to full in the middle and falling, both ends pointed; under it the settings in one scrolling column: Stroke (Spacing 'Continuous', StreamLine 0 %, Taper start 2.0 × size, Taper end 3.0 × size, Taper tip 10 %), Shape (Disc in the ink pill; the stamp settings grey, as a continuous stroke has none), Grain, Paint (Covering), Size, Dynamics; at the bottom Duplicate and Reset, pencil grey: the Inker is as its file has it.
Before changing anything: Back to the list, draw a line on the canvas with the Inker as it is.

Change: tap Inker (chosen: its editor opens at once), drag Taper start to 5: while I hold it a bubble over the knob reads the value; the strip's stroke grows a longer point at its start at once; Reset turns ink. The line on the canvas does not change: drawn strokes keep their look.
Try: draw on the strip with the pen: the stroke uses the Inker as set now and stays; Clear at the strip's corner takes it away. A finger on the strip draws nothing.

Back: the list again, Inker chosen. Undo takes the line away (a brush edit is no undo step, so the edit stays); the same line drawn again starts narrowing over five sizes: the next stroke takes the change.
Reset: tap Inker again: the editor; tap Reset: Taper start reads 2.0 again, the strip shows its first stroke, and Reset is grey.

Duplicate: tap Duplicate: the editor now shows 'Inker copy', a brush of its own with the same values, chosen; Delete stands where Reset stood. Drag Spacing to 40 %: the stroke becomes a row of discs; tap Chalk: chalk stamps 40 % of the size apart, and the shape's settings come alive. Scroll the column with a finger to its end and open Size dynamics: three curve squares, Pressure, Speed and Tilt, each with Reset and what its axis runs from and to; Back to the settings, Back to the list: 'Inker copy' is listed right after Inker with its own picture, chosen.
Draw a stroke on the canvas with the copy: a dotted row of chalk.
Reopen: leave the app and come back: the list still holds Inker copy after Inker, chosen, with its spacing and chalk; the stroke on the canvas is exactly as drawn.
Rename: in the copy's editor tap its name: the Rename brush dialog with the name in its field; type 'Chalk liner' and Done: the heading reads so.
Delete: tap Delete: a dialog asks 'Delete Chalk liner?' (strokes drawn with it stay); Delete: the list without it, Inker chosen. Cancel instead would have kept it.

Failure: no value the engine refuses can be set: every slider stops at its ends, Spacing jumps from Continuous to the least spacing the stamps fit at, the paper keeps a stroke continuous (the shapes grey with why), a curve's points stop where the stamps would not fit. Nothing can fail to save that the toolbox does not already save.
